summary: New intrinsic centre-incidence criterion; complete CE equivalence when restriction is injective inside each centre.
detailedSummary: Universal target CE requires no shared full normalization fibre between distinct centres. Under injectivity of restriction within every centre, CE(R) iff there are no incidence edges and every normal centre has CE. Source CE remains a predicate/hypothesis, with no regular-cover assumption. Proves exact gauge/completion transport and reconstructs geometric curve clipping. Arbitrary same-centre identifications and general normal nonisolated CE remain unresolved.
text:
Use own n2's arbitrary excellent reduced setting. Define a finite incidence graph on the actual normal LOCAL CENTRES: i!=j are joined exactly when rho(Y_i) intersects rho(Y_j). By G331's full infinite-conductor rule, this is equivalent to two centred normalized semivaluations on the corresponding local conductor quotients restricting to the same semivaluation on R/cfrak. Every support and infinite-value quotient point is included. This is an intrinsic boundary test, not a claimed finite effective algorithm on rings.

Let CE(R) mean that every finite continuous signed obstacle on the full primary section has a greatest geometric C_R minorant. Own n1 proves equivalent definitions using greatest D_R minorants, raw continuity or uniform every-degree canonical convergence. Own n2 proves the NEW unconditional necessity:

CE(R) implies that the incidence graph has no edges.

There is no characteristic, smoothness, source-CE or regular-cover condition in this necessity.

NEW COMPLETE SCOPED CRITERION. Assume restriction rho|_(Y_i) is injective inside each individual local centre. Equivalently, the corresponding local conductor quotient restriction is injective on its entire normalized boundary; finite-conductor fibres are already singleton. Then

CE(R) iff [the incidence graph has no edges AND CE(S_i) holds at every normal local centre].

Proof: no edges together with internal injectivity makes rho a continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff full boundaries, hence a homeomorphism. G331's full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives an order isomorphism C_R with the finite product of C_(S_i), and likewise for D. An arbitrary continuous obstacle therefore corresponds to an arbitrary tuple of continuous obstacles, and raw and attained envelopes correspond componentwise. This proves both directions when there are no edges. An edge excludes CE(R) by own n2, proving the equivalence. Whenever the normal centres have CE, internal injectivity leaves precisely the intrinsic incidence test for target CE. No finite regular cover is presumed or constructed, and CE of the normal centres is not proved by this criterion.

The remaining case is explicit. Without internal injectivity, absence of graph edges does not decide identifications WITHIN a single centre. The zero-versus-negative centre separation used in n2 is then unavailable. General normal higher-dimensional nonisolated CE, higher-dimensional positive/mixed-characteristic regular-source CE and arbitrary same-centre conductor classification remain unresolved. This is a new complete scoped criterion and an original-residual bridge, not closure of the unchanged P12.3.

For a new primary ideal b put d(v)=v(b)>0. G331's exact homogeneous transport divides both obstacles and competitors by d(v), which is the same on every full normalization fibre. Taking suprema gives the same transport for raw and attained envelopes. Bounded continuous d and d^(-1) preserve CE and uniform convergence; graph incidence and internal injectivity are gauge independent. Along n2's approaching net d(v_lambda)->d(v_*), so its jump becomes kappa/d(v_*). The granted exact completion boundary homeomorphism and primary-ideal contraction transport the obstruction and CE predicate to completion. No model-category equivalence or generic-degree base-change assertion is made. Nilpotents first reduce away; a zero-dimensional local reduction has the unique empty boundary and empty envelope.

The curve comparison is reconstructed rather than claimed new. An excellent reduced curve has finitely many normal local DVR centres, each with singleton normalized section and finite conductor value. Normalization restriction is therefore a bijection of finite discrete links. Primary powers, unit profiles and positive real scaling give all finite nonpositive values at a DVR; actual decreasing constants give all extended nonpositive values. Semilocal gluing and G331's geometric POSITIVE descent give the downstairs geometric envelope P_R(f)=min(f,0), agreeing with the complete ideal-psh envelope. This conclusion uses the actual Cartier comparison, not merely ideal order calculus. The incidence graph has no edges, consistent with the obstruction theorem.

Literal classical/CLD logarithmic radial extensions remain distinct, with their retained multibranch mixed-zero obstruction. The smooth CLASS specialization remains precisely G331's published smooth affine CLOSED/algebraically closed/characteristic-zero domain and qualified completion; no source-envelope enlargement is inferred. All other G331 qualifications from own n1 remain attached.

Artifacts: n3.tex and P12.3-conductor-centre-obstruction.tex. Rerun: python delivery.py. The criterion is an unverified mathematical conditional classification; artifact checks do not verify its hypotheses or constitute acceptance.
